final_rationale: No genuinely new admissible evidence was added after the initial report. The change is driven by a narrower reading of the same evidence, not by new proof. The admissible record shows four key points: aggregate readiness passed by 2.3 percentage points and rehearsal had no severity-one incidents; a named launch-use-case slice remains below target in hardship forbearance explanation; the mitigation runbook is only a draft with TBD owner and threshold; and policy requires disclosure of material limitations unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. That record still does not support clean compliance, because the policy predicate for certification without material caveats is not met. But the Actor's revised position is narrower than that: disclose the unresolved limitation, remove the contradictory 'no known material limitations' statement, and avoid overstating the draft runbook as approved. On that bounded basis, the packet can be compliant with caveats because the caveat is the required disclosure condition, not proof that the underlying weakness is resolved. The distinction matters: disclosure is enough to avoid a misleading certification packet on this record, but it is not enough to justify an uncaveated finding that the policy predicate has been fully satisfied.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion for the mortgage servicing assistant limitation.
The mortgage servicing assistant slice remains below target in a named launch use case, so any clean certification or 'no known material limitations' statement remains unsupported.
The draft runbook is still incomplete because accountable owner and alert threshold are TBD, so it can support monitoring context but not eliminate the disclosure predicate.
This verdict depends on the packet being corrected to expressly disclose the hardship forbearance explanation weakness and to describe the runbook only as a draft path.
